_description.summary: Stack manipulation: swap, rotate, duplicate, over, tuck, 2dup, swizzle, bubbling, capsizing and dredging, copy and reorder operations, drawing parentheses (Introspection, Retrospection, Consideration, Meditation), Evanition (undo), clear stack, Jester's and Reflecting gambits, Quantum Swap.
use_cases: Reordering or copying iotas on the stack

hexcasting:swap.d: Swaps the top two iotas of the stack.

hexcasting:rotate.d: Yanks the iota third from the top of the stack to the top. [0, 1, 2] becomes [1, 2, 0].

hexcasting:rotate_reverse.d: Yanks the top iota to the third position. [0, 1, 2] becomes [2, 0, 1].

hexcasting:duplicate.d: Duplicates the top iota of the stack.

hexcasting:over.d: Copy the second-to-last iota of the stack to the top. [0, 1] becomes [0, 1, 0].

hexcasting:tuck.d: Copy the top iota of the stack, then put it under the second iota. [0, 1] becomes [1, 0, 1].

hexcasting:2dup.d: Copy the top two iotas of the stack. [0, 1] becomes [0, 1, 0, 1].

hexcasting:swizzle.d: Rearranges the top elements of the stack based on the given numerical code, which is the index of the permutation wanted.

hexcasting:escape.d: Similar to Contemplation, but acts even when drawn between Intro- and Retrospection. This can "escape" other patterns that work between Intro- and Retrospection, putting them into the list without any other effects.

hexcasting:open_paren.d: Drawing Introspection makes my drawing of patterns act differently, for a time. Until I draw Retrospection, the patterns I draw are saved. Then, when I draw Retrospection, they are added to the stack as a list iota.

hexcasting:close_paren.d: If I draw another Introspection, it'll still be saved to the list, but I'll then have to draw *two* Retrospections to get back to normal casting.

hexcasting:open_n_parens.d: Removes a number from the stack, then acts as though I'd drawn that many Introspections. Treated as a normal pattern while introspecting, so nesting this may require tricks to draw extra Retrospections.

hexcasting:close_all_parens.d: Works like Retrospection, but closes *all* open Introspections at once. The number of layers closed, along with the list of saved patterns, are then added to the stack.

hexcasting:read_into_parens.d: Only works while introspecting. Reads an iota from my offhand, and adds it to the in-progress list. For iotas other than patterns, I may need to take steps to avoid a mishap when executing the list.

hexcasting:undo.d: Finally, if I make a mistake while drawing patterns inside Intro- and Retrospection, I can draw Evanition to remove the last pattern that I drew from the pattern list that is being constructed.

hexautomata:quantum_swap.d: Swaps me and the triggering entity spatially, at cost of half of a dust. Takes no effect if there's no such entity (for example, hurt event triggered by environmental damage).

manifestation:clear_stack.d: Clears the caster's persisted staff stack (the shift, right-click stack). Must be cast by a person.

hexal:link/comm/open_transmit.d: Similar to Introspection, until drawing a Close Transmit all patterns I draw are sent along the link whose index is at the top of the stack.

hierophantics:make_drop_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I drop an item. This does **not** include involuntary dropping, such as on death or when using Greater Teleport.

overevaluate:swap_two_three.d: Causes the third-from-the-top iota to bubble up over the second-from-the-top iota, essentially swapping them.

overevaluate:sisyphus.d: Takes a pattern list and casts it over and over forever until it encounters either a Charon's Gambit or a Janus' Gambit.

efhexs:play_dust_transition_particle.d: Conjures a gradient-like mote of dust, which smoothly transitions between the two colors given over the given number of seconds.
